name: pyrosm
what_it_holds: Python library (MIT, 438 stars, ~1,065 commits, Cython-accelerated) that parses OSM .osm.pbf extracts (e.g. Geofabrik regional dumps) directly into GeoPandas GeoDataFrames. Supports custom tag filters (including Overpass-style filters, so `tourism=hotel`/`tourism=guest_house` etc.) plus roads, buildings, land use, and boundaries. v0.10+ adds an out-of-core streaming engine for continental-scale files.
why_useful: Fastest available method to bulk-extract tourism/hotel POIs from Geofabrik country/region extracts for many cities at once, rather than one-by-one Overpass queries — directly serves the 'counting STR/hotel supply from maps' half of this theme.
time_coverage: Current OSM snapshot at pull time (historical PBF snapshots available separately from Geofabrik's internal history server, not this tool)
themes: POI and place data: Overture Maps places, OSM extracts (tourism=*), Foursquare open places, Geofabrik tooling; counting STR/hotel supply from maps
why_all: Fastest available method to bulk-extract tourism/hotel POIs from Geofabrik country/region extracts for many cities at once, rather than one-by-one Overpass queries — directly serves the 'counting STR/hotel supply from maps' half of this theme.

name: nowcasting_benchmark
what_it_holds: Replication code (R and Python notebooks) for 17 nowcasting/forecasting methods run head-to-head: ARMA, Bayesian VAR, DFM, MIDAS, MF-VAR, midasml (econometric); decision trees, elastic net, gradient boost, LSTM, MLP, OLS, RF, ridge/lasso, XGBoost, DeepVAR (ML). Uses FRED-sourced US macro series to nowcast quarterly US GDP, Q1 2002-Q3 2022 (shortened 2005-2010 demo notebooks for runtime). 35 commits, MIT license.
why_useful: A ready reference implementation and honest performance comparison across every mixed-frequency method named in gap #17 (MIDAS, DFM, bridge-style MF-VAR, midasml) — useful to pick and validate the estimation approach for an ABNB KPI nowcast before committing engineering time to one method.
themes: Nowcasting methods and packages: MIDAS, dynamic factor models, bridge equations, nowcasting with Google Trends, KPI nowcasting for companies
why_all: A ready reference implementation and honest performance comparison across every mixed-frequency method named in gap #17 (MIDAS, DFM, bridge-style MF-VAR, midasml) — useful to pick and validate the estimation approach for an ABNB KPI nowcast before committing engineering time to one method.

Directly on-theme: gives runnable code (not just theory) for MIDAS, DFM, MF-VAR, bridge-style comparisons against ML baselines on a mixed-frequency macro target -- a template that could be repointed at ABNB KPI mixed-frequency nowcasting (nights/GBV target with monthly/weekly high-frequency indicators), addressing gap #17.

name: nowcasting-dfm
what_it_holds: Python DFM nowcasting package extending the FRBNY (New York Fed) DFM framework, with a 'Pseudo-Real-Time Synthesizer' (sp_vintage_generator.py) that reconstructs historical ragged-edge/vintage data matrices and maps real release-calendar timing (e.g. 'first Friday of month') to avoid look-ahead bias in backtests; Numba acceleration, Kalman news decomposition, Plotly dashboards. Ships FRED-sourced US macro example series and two spec files (Spec_US_example.xls, Spec_FredMD_2026-07.xlsx). 115 commits, BSD-3-Clause.
why_useful: The vintage/ragged-edge synthesizer is exactly the point-in-time machinery gap #4 asks for (reconstructing what was known as-of a date) and directly usable as a harness for mixed-frequency KPI nowcasting with correct release timing -- more mechanically relevant than most MIDAS/DFM repos found.

name: bridgr
what_it_holds: R package explicitly for classical bridge-equation and MIDAS-style nowcasting: automated frequency alignment (seconds to years), indicator forecasting/aggregation (expalmon, beta weighting), prediction intervals. Ships two example datasets: gdp (quarterly GDP) and baro (monthly business-barometer indicator). 189 commits, MIT license, actively maintained (last update Aug 2026 per topic listing).
why_useful: Purpose-built, current (2026) implementation of bridge equations -- the exact method named in the theme -- with a working monthly-indicator-to-quarterly-target example (barometer survey to GDP) structurally identical to a monthly alt-data indicator bridging to ABNB's quarterly nights/GBV.
